stories.title: Eli and the Word He Did Not Know
stories.outro: See you next time in Sunny Meadow!
stories.moral: Asking what a word means helps you learn what to do.
moralRhyme: When a word feels strange and new,
Ask, and find what you can do!

youtube.title: Eli and the Word He Did Not Know | Sunny Meadow
youtube.description: Eli's buttons landed in three very mixed-up groups. Ozzy paused beside the little sorting table. A gentle friendship story. Asking what a word means helps you learn what to do. #SunnyMeadow #DreamyDiscoveries

lines.text: Eli's buttons landed in three very mixed-up groups.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Ozzy paused beside the little sorting table.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I followed your instruction, but this looks different.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: I asked for sorting. What did that word mean to you?
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Eli had agreed to help prepare their craft box.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He wanted to understand the job before snack time.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I thought sorting might mean spreading them around.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: I should have explained the word before we began.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Eli looked at Ozzy's neat little group of buttons.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He copied its long shape with the next three.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Now my group looks just like your group.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Its shape does, but these buttons have different colors.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Eli rearranged his three buttons into a smaller row.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Ozzy waited without taking the buttons from him.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Maybe sorting means making all the rows smaller.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Not quite. Would you like me to explain another way?
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Does Eli have to pretend he understands?
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Eli felt his ears grow warm with embarrassment.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He had nodded as though he understood the word.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I did not know what sorting meant at all.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Thank you for telling me. We can start there.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Ozzy explained that sorting puts things into groups.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Eli watched the buttons beside his wide little paws.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: We can choose which things belong in each group?
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Yes. Today we chose groups of the same color.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Eli looked at a red button beside a blue one.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He still wanted to see the instruction in action.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Could you show me with just one button?
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: This red one goes beside another red one.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Ozzy moved one button and left the others for Eli.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Eli picked up a second red button himself.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Then this red button belongs beside those two.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Exactly. You chose the group by its color.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Eli placed the blue buttons in their own group.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He kept the yellow ones in the little tray.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I am sorting by color, with three different groups.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: And you are doing the choosing this time.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: What could help explain a new word?
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: One tiny button was red with a yellow middle.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Eli stopped before dropping it into either colored group.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: This one has two colors. Which rule are we using?
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Let us use the color around the outside today.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Eli put the two-colored button with the red ones.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He checked the remaining buttons one at a time.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Now I know how to decide about that tricky one.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Asking made our instruction much clearer for both of us.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: The craft box had three neatly separated button groups.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Eli counted the empty spaces in the old tray.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I finished the job after I understood the word.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: You also helped me give a clearer instruction.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Ozzy asked whether Eli wanted to arrange the ribbons.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Eli looked at two very different ribbon lengths.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Does arrange mean sorting, or choosing where they go?
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Here it means laying them side by side for choosing.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Eli laid the ribbons down without making color groups.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He gave the shortest one a careful little pat.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Excellent. No ribbon has to guess its instructions.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Especially that short one. It looks easily confused.
lines.speaker: friend
